newsitem.title: UK: Scottish university sacks pro-paedophilia lecturer.
newsitem.headline: Scottish university sacks pro-paedophilia lecturer.

text.p: Scotland's Edinburgh University said on Friday it was sacking a controversial psychology lecturer who said there was nothing wrong with paedophilia if the child was intelligent and willing.
The lecturer, Chris Brand, had been suspended in November last year after making the comment in an electronic newsletter on the Internet.

University principal Sir Stewart Sutherland said on Friday that a disciplinary tribunal had found Brand's conduct and public statements disgraceful and incompatible with his duties as a lecturer, and that he would be dismissed immediately.

Sutherland said the sacking had nothing to do with an outcry last year over Brand's book "The g Factor" which said black people were less intelligent than whites. It also claimed single mothers had low intelligence and needed more intelligent lovers.

"Neither I nor my colleagues have sought to censor Mr Brand's researched conclusions on ethnic background and intelligence," Sutherland said. "Indeed we went out of our way to defend his right to express them in a reasoned manner."

Brand, 54, calls himself a "scientific racist". He has taught at the university for more than 25 years but was removed as a director of studies in 1986 after students objecting to his sexist and racist views boycotted his classes and organised alternative lectures and seminars.
